messages:
jamal: FYI customer HydraHealth is seeing a surge of 429s + latency on their Dedicated pool in us-west-2. CS escalated, they say requests queue for ~8-12s then 429. I have logs attached.

anya: thanks — can you paste repro steps and a few example request IDs?

jamal: quick repro: send steady 30 rps for 5m to their route. example request id: hh_req_20260315_0912. Symptoms: token latency spike then 429s. CS link: https://cs.redwood/hydra/incident/5123 :thumbsup:

chris: grabbing scaler + probe traces now. early guess: autoscaler holdoff triggered because probe ack latency spiked; system suppressed further scale attempts for 30s windows.

scale-bot: [ALERT] 2026-03-15T09:12:06Z autoscaler: holdoff_engaged=true reason=probe_failure_rate>0.15 window=30s current_min_replicas=8 desired=24

chris: paste of relevant logs (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] probe-sender: queued=47 inflight=12
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] probe-sender: send(alloc-72): timeout=250ms ack=3020ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] scaler-eval: desired_replicas_calc=24; holdoff=true; holdoff_reason=probe_backpressure
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] kube-events: imagepull_backoff node=ip-10-0-44-12 noisy-tenant=acct-789
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] allocator: attach_latency=4.1s; attach_failures=3
```

anya: interesting — kube imagepull backoffs on the same nodes as high probe latency. that suggests noisy neighbor or node-level IO saturation preventing probe ACKs. autoscaler treat probe timeouts as probe_failure_rate increase -> triggers holdoff to avoid thrashing.

leo-cs: customer reports this started around 09:10 after a deploy of a separate tenant on same pool. they called it "bursting not from our app".

chris: reproducer commands I used (safe):

```
# run 30 RPS against their route for 5 mins
for i in `seq 1 15000`; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}'; sleep 0.033; done
```

anya: short-term mitigation options
- increase min_replicas for HydraHealth pool to 12 (reduce coldstart pressure)
- temporarily disable probe_suppression threshold for the affected pool (risky)
- migrate HydraHealth to a dedicated node pool (isolates noisy tenants)

chris: i've already rolled a temporary increase to min_replicas -> 12 for the pool. watching metrics now.

scale-bot: [ACTION] changed min_replicas for pool hydra-usw2 from 8 -> 12 by chris (reason: customer-impacting 429s).

jamal: customer notified that we're applying mitigations; they'll monitor. thanks. can we capture a reproducible telemetry dump for postmortem?

anya: yes — chris can export probe_histogram, node_io_stats, and autoscaler_event_log window 09:05-09:25. We should also tag the offending tenant and check imagepull frequency.

chris: exporting now. attaching short repro artifacts to the ticket. will also add a dashboard panel for probe_ack_latency and probe_queue_depth.

leo-cs: customer says latency dropped after min_replicas bump. they still want a follow-up on "why autoscaler didn't scale faster".

anya: root cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor caused node-level IO and imagepull thrash -> probe ACK latencies spiked -> autoscaler interpreted as backend instability and engaged conservative holdoff -> desired replicas stalled below demand. Follow-up engineering tasks:
- increase observability on probe path (traces + flamegraphs) @chris
- tune holdoff thresholds (lower duration but smaller penalty) @anya
- policy: require tenant isolation for customers with >X qps spikes. @product

jamal: i'll schedule a customer postmortem call next week. thanks team. :white_check_mark:

anya: created a short ticket: INT-6521 (investigate probe_holdoff oscillation + noisy-tenant imagepull). assigning to eng-ml team.

chris: next steps I will: upload traces, open PR for dashboards, and run a controlled noiseflood on staging to test tuned thresholds. ETA EOD today.

scale-bot: [NOTE] follow-up metrics to watch: probe_ack_p50/p95, autoscaler_holdoff_count, node_imagepull_errors, attach_latency_p95.

jamal: resolving thread in CS but will reopen if customer sees regression. keep me posted.

anya: thanks all — good catch. :pray:
